videos.script: Until now, anybody who could reach shelf could read every book. That is about to change. {{door}} This lesson puts the books behind a door, and asks one question there. Who is this? {{question}} There are three common answers. A name and a password, sent with every request. A token, handed out once after a login. And a key, given to a program rather than to a person. {{three}} You build all three into one small server, and you look at it from the side that defends it. What does the server keep? Never the secret itself, only something that can check it. {{stored}} How does it say no? With a 401 that names the ways in, and the same words for every stranger. {{refusal}} And where does a secret leak? In an address, in a log line, in a comparison that takes a little too long. {{leaks}} At the end, you choose. Which credential fits which caller, and what each one costs when it gets out. {{choose}}
